boundary_rationale: “Yahweh's law is perfect, restoring the soul” (web:Ps.19.7) opens the torah-panel by naming the covenant name יְהוָ֣ה, Yahweh (oshb:Ps.19.8), which recurs seven times across four verses in this panel — web:Ps.19.7, Ps.19.8, Ps.19.9, and Ps.19.14 (sweep: 7 occurrences across 4 verses) — against the one אֵ֑ל token of the panel before it (oshb:Ps.19.2). Three verses of synonym-paired praise for the law (law/covenant at web:Ps.19.7, precepts/commandment at web:Ps.19.8, fear/ordinances at web:Ps.19.9) run through “sweeter also than honey and the extract of the honeycomb” (web:Ps.19.10) before “Moreover your servant is warned by them” (web:Ps.19.11) turns from describing the law's qualities to the psalmist's own response, closing on the prayer formula “Let the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable in your sight, Yahweh, my rock, and my redeemer” (web:Ps.19.14), which readdresses Yahweh directly and closes the psalm.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting this panel at web:Ps.19.10|Ps.19.11 carries a tier-1 rival the one-panel reading does not fully answer: oshb:Ps.19.12 (web:Ps.19.11) carries עַ֭בְדְּךָ (“your servant”) as its second token, after גַּֽם, the psalm’s first second-person form, against the third-person law-description running web:Ps.19.7-Ps.19.10 (oshb:Ps.19.8-Ps.19.11), where no second-person form stands. The one-panel reading holds on the strophe’s ~4-8 verse norm and the unbroken movement from the law’s praise into the closing prayer at web:Ps.19.14, not on the sevenfold divine-name count, which is silent across this seam (zero occurrences at oshb:Ps.19.11-Ps.19.14).
observed_substrate_signals: יְהוָ֣ה (Yahweh) occurs twice each at oshb:Ps.19.8, oshb:Ps.19.9, oshb:Ps.19.10 and once at oshb:Ps.19.15 — seven token-occurrences across four verses (sweep: 7 occurrences across 4 verses)
no divine-name token (Yahweh or El) appears at web:Ps.19.11-Ps.19.13, the personal-response verses between the law's praise and the closing prayer formula
device_notes: No selah interrupts web:Ps.19.7-Ps.19.14; this torah panel and the heavens panel that precedes it remain one composition's two internal movements, not separate parents.

boundary_rationale: Third-person report אֱלֹהִ֤ים דִּבֶּ֥ר (oshb:Ps.60.8), “God has spoken from his sanctuary” (web:Ps.60.6), introduces a first-person divine oracle sustained by אֶ֫עְלֹ֥זָה and אֲחַלְּקָ֥ה (oshb:Ps.60.8) through אַשְׁלִ֣יךְ (oshb:Ps.60.10): “I will divide Shechem, and measure out the valley of Succoth” (web:Ps.60.6), “Gilead is mine, and Manasseh is mine” (web:Ps.60.7), closing “I shout in triumph over Philistia” (web:Ps.60.8). The oracle’s first-person divine voice closes at oshb:Ps.60.10; oshb:Ps.60.11 opens interrogative on a 1cs object, מִ֣י יֹ֭בִלֵנִי, whose speaker can no longer be God, and oshb:Ps.60.12 makes the shift explicit in second-person address to God, הֲלֹֽא אַתָּ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֣ים זְנַחְתָּ֑נוּ.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending the direct divine speech through web:Ps.60.9 (oshb:Ps.60.11), as the oracle’s recurrence in Psalm 108 might imply at a glance, was rejected because oshb:Ps.60.11 opens interrogative with a 1cs object, מִ֣י יֹ֭בִלֵנִי, whose speaker can no longer be the oracle’s first-person Yahweh, and oshb:Ps.60.12 makes the shift explicit in second-person address to God, הֲלֹֽא אַתָּ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֣ים זְנַחְתָּ֑נוּ.
observed_substrate_signals: The oracle’s sustained first-person divine forms — אֶ֫עְלֹ֥זָה and אֲחַלְּקָ֥ה (oshb:Ps.60.8) through אַשְׁלִ֣יךְ (oshb:Ps.60.10) — close at oshb:Ps.60.10, against the interrogative 1cs-object opening of oshb:Ps.60.11 (מִ֣י יֹ֭בִלֵנִי) and the explicit 2ms address of oshb:Ps.60.12 (הֲלֹֽא אַתָּ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֣ים זְנַחְתָּ֑נוּ), where the speaker can no longer be God.
Third-person speech-report noun+verb opens the span: (oshb:Ps.60.8) אֱלֹהִ֤ים דִּבֶּ֥ר (‘God has spoken’), introducing the quoted first-person oracle that follows.
device_notes: This oracle recurs, with real textual differences rather than exact repetition, in Psalm 108 (the Ps 57+60=108 doublet) — a typed cross-psalm relation, not a merged row; collation checked directly against Psalm 108's text reaches accent_stripped as its highest tier (on 1 of the 3 verse pairs), down to no shared tier on the others, verse by verse.

boundary_rationale: The title is one counted MT verse (web:Ps.62.0 = oshb:Ps.62.1), naming the Jeduthun setting (one of 3 Ps psalms so labeled, with Psalms 39 and 77). The unit is a ring: it opens on (oshb:Ps.62.2) אַ֣ךְ אֶל אֱ֭לֹהִים דּֽוּמִיָּ֣ה “My soul rests in God alone” (web:Ps.62.1), turns at web:Ps.62.3 to a complaint against attackers, “How long will you assault a man?”, and returns to the same confidence idiom at (oshb:Ps.62.6) אַ֣ךְ לֵ֭אלֹהִים דּ֣וֹמִּי נַפְשִׁ֑י “My soul, wait in silence for God alone, for my expectation is from him.” (web:Ps.62.5), completing the envelope. Collated against oshb:Ps.62.6, oshb:Ps.62.2 shares no tier — real lexical substitution: (oshb:Ps.62.2) אֶל אֱ֭לֹהִים against (oshb:Ps.62.6) לֵ֭אלֹהִים, and (oshb:Ps.62.2) יְשׁוּעָתִֽי against (oshb:Ps.62.6) תִּקְוָתִֽי — so the return is thematic anaphora (sweep: 6 verses open with אך in Ps 62, 34 book-wide), not a repeated line.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the ring at its individual אך-openings into separate one- or two-verse rows was rejected, since the confidence-complaint-confidence pattern needs the full envelope to complete, not one opening on its own.
observed_substrate_signals: אך opens (oshb:Ps.62.2) אַ֣ךְ, oshb:Ps.62.3, and (oshb:Ps.62.5) אַ֤ךְ inside this row, plus 2 more later in the psalm: 6 verse-initial occurrences of אך among Ps 62’s 12 MT body verses; a separate contiguous-consonantal-substring sweep finds 34 occurrences book-wide.

oshb:Ps.62.3 opens with אַךְ ה֣וּא צ֭וּרִי וִֽישׁוּעָתִ֑י מִ֝שְׂגַּבִּ֗י, echoed at this row’s own closing verse, oshb:Ps.62.7 (=web:Ps.62.6), whose opening five tokens repeat oshb:Ps.62.3 byte-for-byte; oshb:Ps.62.3 carries two further tokens beyond that match (לֹא אֶמּ֥וֹט רַבָּֽה) that oshb:Ps.62.7 lacks.
Selah closes web:Ps.62.4 (oshb:Ps.62.5), mid-ring rather than at the row’s own end — disclosed, not treated as the driver.
device_notes: This row family has Psalm 62 for its parent.

boundary_rationale: Psalm 78 opens with a maskil superscription (“A contemplation by Asaph.”, web:Ps.78.0) sitting inside the same MT verse as the psalm's opening imperative, then unfolds one continuous wisdom exordium: the call “Hear my teaching, my people. Turn your ears to the words of my mouth.” (web:Ps.78.1) sets a teacher's address that a purpose-clause chain develops — the covenant-transmission command of web:Ps.78.5, extended by “that the generation to come might know…who should arise and tell their children” (web:Ps.78.6) and “that they might set their hope in God, and not forget God's deeds, but keep his commandments” (web:Ps.78.7) — until it resolves in a negative exemplar, “and might not be as their fathers- a stubborn and rebellious generation, a generation that didn't make their hearts loyal, whose spirit was not steadfast with God.” (web:Ps.78.8). The unnamed “fathers” of web:Ps.78.8 are then given a specific referent at web:Ps.78.9, marking the seam.
strongest_rejected_alternative: A break after web:Ps.78.4’s transmission pledge was considered but rejected because oshb:Ps.78.5’s wayyiqtol וַיָּ֤קֶם is a consecutive form binding it to what precedes rather than opening an independent new movement, and because the transmission vocabulary of oshb:Ps.78.4 — לְד֥וֹר אַחֲר֗וֹן, מְֽ֭סַפְּרִים, מִבְּנֵיהֶ֗ם — recurs across the seam in דּ֣וֹר אַ֭חֲרוֹן, וִֽיסַפְּר֥וּ and לִבְנֵיהֶֽם (also closing oshb:Ps.78.5 as לִבְנֵיהֶֽם) through oshb:Ps.78.5-Ps.78.6, and the purpose-clause chain then runs from oshb:Ps.78.6 to the negative exemplar at web:Ps.78.8.
observed_substrate_signals: the superscription מַשְׂכִּ֗יל לְאָ֫סָ֥ף (web:Ps.78.0 = oshb:Ps.78.1, byte tier) sits inside MT v1 before the body clause הַאֲזִ֣ינָה עַ֭מִּי תּוֹרָתִ֑י (oshb:Ps.78.1, byte tier), consistent with this psalm's identity numbering

the purpose-clause particle opening web:Ps.78.6 (לְמַ֤עַן, oshb:Ps.78.6, byte tier) chains forward from the covenant-commission of web:Ps.78.5; web:Ps.78.7 continues the same purpose clause on a plain waw-conjunctive verb (וְיָשִׂ֥ימוּ, oshb:Ps.78.7, byte tier) rather than opening a fresh particle of its own
web:Ps.78.8 closes on an unnamed collective (“their fathers”) that web:Ps.78.9 immediately specifies by tribal name — a subject change unlike any within web:Ps.78.1-web:Ps.78.8
device_notes: Psalm 78's title carries the maskil and le-Asaph genre labels (web:Ps.78.0 = oshb:Ps.78.1).

boundary_rationale: The maskil-le-Ethan title heads the psalm (מַ֝שְׂכִּ֗יל לְאֵיתָ֥ן הָֽאֶזְרָחִֽי, web:Ps.89.0 = oshb:Ps.89.1) and the opening verse states the composition’s own double topic — “I will sing of the loving kindness of Yahweh forever” (web:Ps.89.1) — before the psalmist’s declaration turns, at 89:3, into a quoted first-person divine oath: “I have made a covenant with my chosen one, I have sworn to David, my servant” (web:Ps.89.3). The unit closes on that oath’s own guarantee, “I will establish your offspring forever, and build up your throne to all generations” (web:Ps.89.4), corroborated by Selah (web:Ps.89.4 = oshb:Ps.89.5).
strongest_rejected_alternative: A rival reading closes the unit at web:Ps.89.2 (oshb:Ps.89.3) and opens the next at web:Ps.89.3 (oshb:Ps.89.4), where oshb:Ps.89.3 closes in the psalmist's own second-person address to Yahweh, תָּכִ֖ן אֱמוּנָתְךָ֣ בָהֶֽם, and oshb:Ps.89.4 opens in Yahweh's own first-person oath, כָּרַ֣תִּֽי בְ֭רִית לִבְחִירִ֑י — a genuine speaker shift this candidate discloses rather than resolves, Selah at web:Ps.89.4 (oshb:Ps.89.5) corroborating a close there only as tier-3 evidence, not the ground for holding the oath inside this unit.
observed_substrate_signals: superscription genre label maskil + attribution le-Ethan opens the psalm (tier-1)
first-person vow (89:1-2) shifts into quoted divine oath at 89:3, the closing 2ms-suffixed שָׁמַ֓יִם תָּכִ֖ן אֱמוּנָתְךָ֣ (oshb:Ps.89.3) turning to the 1cs כָּרַ֣תִּֽי בְ֭רִית (oshb:Ps.89.4)
Selah closes the unit at web:Ps.89.4 = oshb:Ps.89.5 (tier-3 corroboration)
device_notes: Psalm 89 is a single composition; every row here shares one parent, Psalm 89, from title to closing doxology. Selah corroborates this unit’s close (web:Ps.89.4 = oshb:Ps.89.5).

boundary_rationale: The psalm opens in third-person description, “He who dwells…” (web:Ps.91.1), before the voice turns to first-person confession, “I will say of…” (web:Ps.91.2). The second-person address that opens at web:Ps.91.3 (יַ֭צִּֽילְךָ, oshb:Ps.91.3) has not yet begun, so the third-person description and its first-person confession stand together as one unit before the address begins.
strongest_rejected_alternative: web:Ps.91.3 shifts both grammatical person and addressee, opening the protective second-person address that governs the rest of the psalm rather than continuing the speaker's own confession, so folding it into this row was rejected.
observed_substrate_signals: oshb:Ps.91.1's opening participle יֹ֭שֵׁב (oshb:Ps.91.1, 'dwells') names a generic figure, not an addressed 'you'

the person chain moves from the masculine-singular participle יֹ֭שֵׁב, whose clause is resumed by the 3ms יִתְלוֹנָֽן (oshb:Ps.91.1), to the 1cs forms אֹמַ֗ר and אֶבְטַח (oshb:Ps.91.2) to the 2ms-suffixed יַ֭צִּֽילְךָ (oshb:Ps.91.3), where the second-person address begins
device_notes: Rows of Psalm 91 group to one parent unit.

boundary_rationale: oshb:Ps.91.13 closes on the second-person address תִּרְמֹ֖ס כְּפִ֣יר וְתַנִּֽין (oshb:Ps.91.13), and web:Ps.91.14 opens with the causal clause כִּ֤י בִ֣י חָ֭שַׁק וַאֲפַלְּטֵ֑הוּ (oshb:Ps.91.14, 'because he has clung to me and I will deliver him'), a first-person divine verb shifting the speaker from the second-person address-voice of oshb:Ps.91.3-Ps.91.13 to Yahweh's own voice, sustained by אֲ֝שַׂגְּבֵ֗הוּ (oshb:Ps.91.14), וְֽאֶעֱנֵ֗הוּ (oshb:Ps.91.15) and אַשְׂבִּיעֵ֑הוּ (oshb:Ps.91.16). This closing oracle, in which God speaks of the trusting individual in the third person ('him'), is a distinct unit from the second-person address that precedes it.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating web:Ps.91.13 as the oracle's opening verse was rejected because it still addresses 'you' in the second person, while web:Ps.91.14 is where Yahweh's own first-person voice begins.
observed_substrate_signals: the verb וַאֲפַלְּטֵ֑הוּ (oshb:Ps.91.14, 'and I will deliver him') is first-person, first-person divine speech -- Yahweh's own voice, distinct in speaker from the third-person and second-person address of the rest of the psalm, though not the psalm's only first-person verb -- 2 occurrences (אֹמַ֗ר/אֶבְטַח) recur at oshb:Ps.91.2, also 1cs
device_notes: The closing oracle carries the psalm's direct divine first-person speech, distinct in voice from its other three spans.

boundary_rationale: A new wayyiqtol verb introduces a new named subject: “Israel also came into Egypt” (web:Ps.105.23) — MT reads 'וַיָּבֹ֣א יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל מִצְרָ֑יִם' (oshb:Ps.105.23) — turning from Joseph individually to Israel corporately. “He increased his people greatly” (web:Ps.105.24) and “turned their heart to hate his people” (web:Ps.105.25) set up the oppression that “He sent Moses, his servant, and Aaron” answers (web:Ps.105.26), the Hebrew 'שָׁ֭לַח מֹשֶׁ֣ה עַבְדּ֑וֹ' at oshb:Ps.105.26; the unit closes with Moses and Aaron performing “miracles among them, and wonders in the land of Ham” (web:Ps.105.27), the general statement the plague catalogue itemizes from 105:28.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending the unit through the whole nine-verse plague list was considered, but 105:28 opens the itemized catalogue proper with its own perfect verb ('שָׁ֣לַֽח', roughly 'he sent [darkness],' oshb:Ps.105.28 — a ketiv/qere note sits later in this verse per pmarks_Ps.json kq, not quoted here), where 105:27 still speaks in the general terms (“miracles… wonders”, web:Ps.105.27) that the catalogue then specifies.
observed_substrate_signals: new wayyiqtol verb with new named subject Israel opens the unit (105:23), narrative-subject shift from Joseph
unit runs population growth → oppression → the sending of Moses/Aaron → a general miracles/wonders statement that the following catalogue itemizes
device_notes: The plague sequence itemized from 105:28-36 names 9 distinct plague nouns in the psalm's own bytes: darkness (חֹ֭שֶׁךְ, oshb:Ps.105.28), blood (לְדָ֑ם, oshb:Ps.105.29), frogs (צְפַרְדְּעִ֑ים, oshb:Ps.105.30), swarming things and lice (עָרֹ֑ב and כִּ֝נִּ֗ים, oshb:Ps.105.31), hail (בָּרָ֑ד, oshb:Ps.105.32 — 10 if אֵ֖שׁ לֶהָב֣וֹת in the same verse is counted as its own object rather than the hail's accompaniment), locusts and young locusts (אַרְבֶּ֑ה and וְ֝יֶ֗לֶק, oshb:Ps.105.34), and the firstborn (בְּכ֣וֹר, oshb:Ps.105.36); a cross-book relation to Exodus's narrative noted as texture, not boundary authority for these rows.
